newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China and Britain argue over flags, paper says.
newsitem.headline: China and Britain argue over flags, paper says.

text.p: Britain and China have settled an argument over the sequence in which flags should be raised and lowered at the ceremony to hand back Hong Kong to Beijing's rule at midnight on June 30, a newspaper said on Monday.

"Flap over flags at handover settled," said a headline in the South China Morning Post, which added that agreement on the issue was reached by the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group, the body handling details of the transition.
A government spokeswoman declined to say whether there had been a dispute, but cited a document from the Joint Liaison Group last September listing agreed arrangements.
Immediately before midnight on June 30, the British national anthem will be played and the British and Hong Kong flags lowered, the document said.
Immediately after midnight the Chinese anthem will be played as the flags of China and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, as the territory will be called, are raised.
The new Hong Kong flag bears an image of the territory's official flower, the bauhinia, which is already used on Hong Kong coins in place of a profile of Britain's Queen Elizabeth.
The South China Morning Post, quoting a pro-China source, said Britain had wanted the Hong Kong flag lowered first, followed by the British flag, "underlining a dignified retreat from the colony".
Then, according to the British view, the new Hong Kong should be raised followed by the five-starred Chinese banner, the newspaper said.
But the Chinese objected and several other arrangements were debated before an accord was reached under which the British and old Hong Kong flags are lowered simultaneously, it added.

The process of sorting out the transfer of sovereignty of the territory of 6.4 million people has dragged along slowly since Britain and China signed an accord on the handover in 1984. Agreement on issues big and small has often been elusive.
